title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative:
The ICSP Programme, implemented by Trócaire and partners in the Matabeleland South and Masvingo provinces of Zimbabwe, works towards the goal that poor and marginalised people, especially women and youth, have sustainable livelihoods and diverse food sources. This objective focuses on increasing the adoption of agroecological approaches at household and community levels. Activities include agroecology training; food preservation and storage support; and facilitating women and youth farmers in farmer led seed sovereignty movements. The principal focus of this outcome is: • Strengthening the resilience of poor and marginalised people, especially women and youth, through promotion of diverse climate resilient agriculture for food and nutrition security including the adoption of agroecological approaches, seed sovereignty, improved food storage and preservation, and agrobiodiversity, soil conservation measures and trees on farms. • Community-led food and nutrition security analysis and planning using the 6 UN Dimensions of Food Security.
It incorporates the co-creation and sharing of knowledge that enables farmers to adapt to their changing local conditions and to increase their resilience by reducing and adapting to the impacts of climate change and environmental degradation.
This work contributes to the availability of diverse food sources in target communities, and in turn, to improved nutrition outcomes.
